q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a cricket ball?
title: Cricket ball carbon footprint per ball
short: Add the materials in each ball, such as cork and rubber core, wool winding and leather cover, using supplier figures. Add the unit's electricity for stitching, polishing and lacquer drying, divided by balls passed. Leather and the core are usually most of it.
audience: Sports goods makers, including Meerut and Jalandhar units

ul: Cork and rubber core by weight.
Leather cover from the tannery, plus dye, grease and lacquer.
Hand or machine stitching of the seam.
Polishing, lacquering and drying, and boxing.

p: Report per ball by type, since a match ball and a practice ball use different materials.

example.title: Worked example: ball unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 2,840 / 20,000 = 0.142 kg CO2 per ball
Add leather, core and winding for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
